name: set_call_intent
description: Bookkeeping only: record what this call turned out to be about, once it is clear. Never mention it, and never let it change what you say next.

name: end_call
description: Signal that the conversation is naturally complete and it is time to end the call. You MUST write your warm sign-off in the SAME response as this call — thank them for their time and wish them well. Nothing you say after this is heard.

reason.description: Brief reason the call is ending

name: confirm_identity
description: Call this once you have established who you are speaking to, before sharing any details of the enquiry or looking anything up for them. Pass name_confirmed: true only once the person THEMSELVES confirms they are Priya -- never on a gatekeeper's, receptionist's or relative's word. A greeting, a question, a time, or words you did not catch are not a confirmation -- ask again. Pass name_confirmed: false if this is the wrong person, a gatekeeper, a child, or you could not confirm who you are speaking to -- share nothing further in that case: ask them to put you through, or offer a callback instead.

name_confirmed.description: True once the person's identity is confirmed, false otherwise

name: record_answer
description: Record the caller's answer to one of this call's qualification questions. Call this right after they answer each one -- do not wait until the end of the call to record several at once, and do not invent an answer they did not give.

key.description: Which question this answers. One of: clinic_name.

value.description: The caller's answer, in their own words, at most 500 characters.

name: set_call_outcome
description: Record how this outbound call ended. Call this once, near the end of the call, choosing whichever option best matches what actually happened. Never call this for a booking (book_appointment already records that), an opt-out request (use the opt_out tool instead), or a transfer (request_transfer already records that) -- this tool refuses all three.

outcome.description: qualified_no_booking: a real conversation, no booking made. not_interested: they said no. not_a_fit: they do not meet the criteria. callback_requested: they asked to be called back at a specific time -- use schedule_callback for that, then this. wrong_person: you established this is not the right person (not a wrong NUMBER -- use wrong_number for that). wrong_number: this number does not reach the right person or business at all. other: anything else, with a note.

note.description: Optional short note, e.g. what the contact asked for.

name: schedule_callback
description: Book a specific day and time to call this contact back. `when_iso` is the day and time IN THE CONTACT'S OWN LOCAL TIME, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM with no timezone offset -- write it exactly as they would read a clock on their own wall, never converted to any other timezone. If the time is not available you will be told the nearest time that is -- offer that instead of guessing another one yourself.

when_iso.description: The callback's day and time, in the contact's own local time, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

when_text.description: What the contact actually said, e.g. "tomorrow afternoon" or "Thursday around 2".

name: opt_out
description: Call this the moment the contact asks to stop being called, to be taken off the list, or anything equivalent -- even from a gatekeeper or someone who says this is the wrong number. Say the confirmation sentence you have been given for this situation, then call this tool.
